finding.claim: Unauthenticated PasswordHash and LocalUserLogin requests share a 10-slot argon2 semaphore, and a full semaphore makes the call fail with ErrArgon2Busy. An unauthenticated attacker can keep all slots occupied and make legitimate local logins fail intermittently with ResourceExhausted. No per-IP or per-user throttling exists on this path. Severity is low: it needs a sustained flood and it is an availability-only impact.
finding.source: Unauthenticated Connect RPC calls to PasswordHash (any password string) or LocalUserLogin (any username/password). Neither handler requires authentication.
finding.sink: comparePasswordAndHash and CreateHash acquire argon2Sem (capacity 10, non-blocking). When the semaphore is full they return ErrArgon2Busy, which LocalUserLogin turns into connect.CodeResourceExhausted.

trace.note: PasswordHash handler has no auth or ACL check; calls createHash(req.Msg.Password)
argon2MaxConcurrent = 10, one global semaphore shared by hashing and login verification
CreateHash takes a slot for each request; argon2id with 64MiB memory and 4 iterations is slow
comparePasswordAndHash uses the same semaphore and returns ErrArgon2Busy when it is full
LocalUserLogin maps ErrArgon2Busy to CodeResourceExhausted, so the real user's login is rejected

finding.guards_checked: Checked the semaphore bound (it limits memory use but is shared with login). Checked for rate limiting, IP throttling, or auth on PasswordHash (none found). Checked that LocalUserLogin returns early only when local auth is disabled or the user has no password (api.go:229-240); otherwise it reaches the semaphore. The generated proto/connect code is not in this checkout, so I could not check interceptors or middleware.
